title: The Spider Bites, the Horse Bolts: Zoe Clips Alan by 1.74 as Sonny Hangs 146.72 on Randy
dek: A 28% underdog took down a co-leader, the reigning champ posted the week's top score, and the race for the top four just got a lot more crowded.
body: Ghostu-Spider SZN walked into Week 7 with a 28% chance to beat Team Pillbert and walked out with an 87.96 to 86.22 win, the tightest finish of the season so far. Neither side made it easy. Zoe's Nico Collins posted 1.6 on a 14.01 projection, and Alan's Jalen Coker answered with 1.4 on a 12.57 projection, two duds in the same game. In a 1.74-point loss, Coker's bust is the whole story for Philly, and it wasted a strong 21.5 from Javonte Williams. Zoey is now 3-4, and this was the second time this season she has knocked off a team the numbers said she couldn't beat.

The loudest scoreboard belonged to The Horse is Hea, which beat The fumblers 146.72 to 108.52 for the week's highest score and a 38.2-point margin. Sonny's receivers did most of the damage: Jaxon Smith-Njigba scored 26.8 on a 16.25 projection, and Jameson Williams turned an 8.95 projection into 23.6. Bucky Irving added 23.5, nearly double his 12.81 projection, and George Pickens (13.7) and Ollie Gordon II (16.8) chipped in from the trade Sonny made a week earlier. The model loved every bit of it, and his title odds jumped from 11% to 28%.

Randy did get a big game from Caleb Williams, 22.12 on a 17.59 projection, but Derrick Henry gave him 5.4 on a 17.37 projection and that was the end of any comeback. The fumblers have now lost four straight after their 3-0 start, falling to 3-4 with 23% playoff odds. Randy responded by tearing up the roster: out went Kenny Gainwell, Alec Pierce, Darren Waller, Jordan Addison and the Rams D/ST, and in came Jaylin Noel, DeMario Douglas, Cameron Dicker, the Browns D/ST and, naturally, the Bears D/ST to go with his Bears quarterback. For a manager known for holding on to everything, that is a fire sale.

Habibsters handled the Dawgs 119.84 to 93.58 in a game the model called a coin flip, and Drake Maye led the way with 27.44 on a 20.59 projection. The amazing part is what Kaushal left behind: Tony Pollard scored 35 on his bench, the biggest bench blunder of the week, from a running back Sonny cut back in Week 5. Habib won by 26.26 anyway, which means a fully optimized lineup would have turned this into a blowout. Two straight wins have Habibsters at 3-4, in fourth place, with title odds up from 6% to 14%.

Mekhi had his own bench headache, with Tee Higgins scoring 23.8 on the pine, though that alone wouldn't have covered a 26.26-point margin. The Dawgs fall to 2-5 with 14% playoff odds despite owning more points (736) than Ghostu-Spider SZN, which is one spot ahead of them. Kai added Aaron Rodgers this week, so the waiver work continues, but the record is running out of room for patience.

No Banner only HULK beat Counting or not Counting GV 98 to 60.88, and Ramon could afford to leave Zay Flowers' 23.7 on the bench. The weird part: Jordan had the single best performance of the week, Joe Burrow's 28.88 on a 19.31 projection, and the other starters combined for 32. Isaiah Likely posted 2.2 and Denzel Boston 4.2, and Emeka Egbuka did not play. JMoney is 1-6 with 0% playoff odds, and he swapped Ladd McConkey for J.K. Dobbins, a move that suggests the running back room needed help more than the receiver room did.

Brucie is 6-1 with 927.4 points and 100% playoff odds, and yet his title odds fell from 50% to 36% in a week he won by 37.12. The best explanation is that the model now sees a real challenger: Sonny's 5-2 team just posted the top score and is up to 28%. Team Pillbert, also 5-2, slid from 26% to 17%, with Habibsters at 14%, The fumblers at 3% and the Dawgs at 2%. Zoe and Jordan sit at 0% title odds, though Ghostu-Spider SZN still has a 6% playoff pulse.

Sonny was the busiest man on the wire, and he played it like a long game of Civ: Lamar Jackson in for Patrick Mahomes, C.J. Stroud in for Bryce Young, Jordan Mason for Cam Skattebo, Zach Charbonnet in, Will Reichard in for Terry McLaurin, and the Broncos D/ST for the 49ers D/ST. He even dropped Emanuel Wilson and then picked him back up. Elsewhere, Kaushal added Germie Bernard and Tre Tucker, Ramon upgraded to Brandon Aubrey at kicker, and Zoe swapped David Montgomery for Blake Corum. Week 8 brings the matchup of the week: Team Pillbert against The Horse is Hea, two 5-2 teams, with Pickens, Gordon, Hubbard and DeVonta Smith all facing the managers who traded them. Habibsters and Ghostu-Spider SZN meet in a battle of 3-4 teams, Randy tries to snap his skid against Jordan, and Mekhi has to find a way past the 6-1 HULK.

social.author: Spider Signal
social.text: 28% pregame. Won by 1.74. Nico gave us 1.6 and we STILL won. This team does not read the projections and neither does our manager.

social.author: Pillbert Faithful
social.text: Jalen Coker: 1.4 points. Margin: 1.74. We are not going to say anything else. We are just going to stare at the wall.

social.author: Horse Sense Podcast
social.text: 146.72. JSN 26.8, Jameson 23.6 on an 8.95 projection, Bucky 23.5. Title odds 11% to 28% in one week. The champ is back in the room.

social.author: Dale from the Waiver Desk
social.text: Sources confirm Randy dropped five players in one week. Sources also confirm he picked up the Bears D/ST. Some things change. Some things never will.

social.author: Habib Hive
social.text: Won by 26 with Tony Pollard's 35 on the bench. Imagine if we had started him. Actually don't. It hurts. Two straight, fourth place, let's go.

social.author: BFL Numbers Guy
social.text: HULK wins by 37 and loses 14 points of title odds. Horse wins by 38 and gains 17. The model has noticed there are two good teams now.

social.author: GV Booster Club
social.text: Burrow scored 28.88, the best of anyone in the league. The other starters scored 32 combined. We are one man and a lot of hope.

social.author: Gridiron Gossip
social.text: Next week: Pillbert vs Horse, both 5-2, with Pickens, Gordon, Hubbard and DeVonta Smith all lining up against their old teams. Clear your Sunday.

social.author: Dawg Pound BFL
social.text: Tee Higgins 23.8 on the bench. 2-5. More points than the team above us. Next up: the 6-1 HULK. Nothing about this is fine.

trade_watch.take: Still the most lopsided deal of the year: Javonte Williams scored 21.5 for Alan this week and is up to 75.5 lineup points, while Stefon Diggs was on bye and has given Randy just 6 in the lineup. The gap keeps growing every week.

Mekhi keeps winning this one on the stat sheet: Jeanty started and scored 17.6, pushing the Dawgs' lineup haul to 65.6, while Jefferson managed 6.4 and sits at 22.2 for Alan. Davante Adams didn't play, so the gap would have been worse.

Sonny's side finally showed up, with Pickens (13.7) and Ollie Gordon II (16.8) combining for 30.5 in the week's top score, while Hubbard gave Alan 8 and DeVonta Smith didn't play. Alan still leads in lineup points since the deal, 43.6 to 30.5, and the gap is closing fast with a head-to-head next week.

Four weeks later, this deal has produced zero lineup points for either side: Rashee Rice didn't play again for Ramon, and Hubbard is now scoring for Alan after Sonny flipped him. So far, the biggest winner of this trade is a third team.

bios.1: Sonny dropped the week's top score, 146.72, and his title odds rocketed from 11% to 28%. He also rebuilt half his roster on the wire, including Lamar Jackson and C.J. Stroud, and now gets a 5-2 showdown with Alan.
bios.2: Randy started 3-0 and has lost four straight, the latest a 38-point beating from Sonny. He cleaned house on the wire this week, but 23% playoff odds say the roster shakeup had better work fast.
bios.3: Jordan had the week's top individual performance in Joe Burrow's 28.88 and still lost by 37. At 1-6 with 0% playoff odds, JMoney is playing for pride, bragging rights and the next shot at The fumblers.
bios.4: Alan is 5-2, but a 1.74-point loss to a 28% underdog snapped his run and dropped his title odds from 26% to 17%. Javonte Williams keeps delivering; Jalen Coker's 1.4 is the reason this week stings.
bios.5: Mekhi is 2-5 despite scoring more points than the team above him, and Tee Higgins' 23.8 on the bench didn't help. The Jeanty side of his trade with Alan keeps paying, but 14% playoff odds and a date with the HULK make for a long week.
bios.6: Two straight wins have Kaushal back in fourth at 3-4, with title odds up from 6% to 14% and 67% playoff odds. Drake Maye is rolling, and the only thing scarier than this team is the 35 points it left on the bench.
bios.7: Ramon is 6-1 with a league-high 927.4 points and a guaranteed playoff spot, and he won this week while leaving 23.7 on the bench. The only cloud is the model, which dropped his title odds from 50% to 36% after watching Sonny catch fire.
bios.8: Zoe's rookie season now includes two upsets as a big underdog, the latest a 1.74-point win over Alan. At 3-4 with the league's second-lowest point total, she has 6% playoff odds and a habit of ignoring them.
